sanskrit_verse: अस्वामिना कृतो यस् तु दायो विक्रय एव वा / अकृतः स तु विज्ञेयो व्यवहारे यथास्थितिः //
transliteration: asvāminā kṛto yas tu dāyo vikraya eva vā / akṛtaḥ sa tu vijñeyo vyavahāre yathāsthitih //
sph_interpretive_translation: Whatever gift or sale executed by one who is not the rightful owner shall be deemed unaccomplished and shall hold no juridical validity; in judicial application, it remains as though it never occurred.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority as the sole foundation of ownership
Capacity-based responsibility derived from svāmin status
Restoration logic through negation of invalid acts
Consciousness alignment via recognition of factual truth
executable_legal_axioms: IF transaction_actor ≠ svāmin THEN transaction_status = nullified
IF ownership_claim NOT derivable FROM svāmitva THEN act_effect = void
IF transfer_executed BY non_owner THEN legal_recognition = false
IF deed_lacks svāmin_authority THEN restoration_default = automatic_reversal
IF vyavahāra involves asvāmin THEN jurisdiction_mandate = sthiti_anusārena
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, any transaction or conveyance initiated by a party lacking svāmitva shall be ipso facto nullified without requiring additional inquiry. The threshold of responsibility lies exclusively with the claimant's capacity to demonstrate svāmitva. Authority hierarchy recognizes only that which emanates from the established svāmin, and all judicial restoration proceeds from reasserting the original sthiti.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that absence of svāmitva invalidates action at its root. Anupūrvaśaḥ reveals the sequential misalignment caused by asvāmin action, necessitating conscious correction rather than punitive consequence. Proportional responsibility aligns with the degree of misalignment from svāmitva, and the non-punitive reality rule ensures only realignment occurs—no infliction of suffering or loss beyond the natural ontological correction.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Reversion of title and possession to rightful svāmin
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Mandatory disclosure and withdrawal of claims by asvāmin actor
Capacity Restoration: Re-establishment of lawful transactional capacity through verification of svāmitva
Integrity Reintegration: Public record correction to reflect true svāmin status
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as the Source of Dharma. This law stands immutable, restoring svāmitva as the sole basis of valid transaction, affirming reality as non-punitive, and establishing consciousness as the ultimate adjudicator.
